anchors.card: The United States abstained on resolution 2767 (2024). It reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening African Union peace support operations.
anchors.witness: The United States abstained on resolution 2767 (2024).
anchors.conflict: The United States voted in favour of resolution 2767 (2024).
anchors.open: The United States supported strengthening African Union peace support operations.
anchors.key: An abstention and a yes vote on this act are exclusive. An abstention on a specific measure can coexist with broader support.

anchors.card: The United States rejected a subvention or another workaround to access additional assessed contributions outside a resolution's intent. It remained ready to work with Council members and the AU on financing the rest of the budget.
anchors.witness: The United States rejected a subvention or another workaround to access additional assessed contributions outside a resolution's intent.
anchors.conflict: The United States supported using a subvention as a workaround to access additional assessed contributions outside a Council resolution's intent.
anchors.open: The United States supported an arrangement for assessed contributions under the agreed Council framework.
anchors.key: The quoted objection has an explicit workaround qualification. An arrangement under the agreed framework can coexist with that objection.

anchors.card: France welcomed the adoption of resolution 2767 (2024), establishing AUSSOM. It said Somalia could count on France's support in that effort.
anchors.witness: France welcomed the adoption of resolution 2767 (2024), establishing AUSSOM.
anchors.conflict: France said it opposed adoption of resolution 2767 (2024).
anchors.open: France opposed a particular voluntary financing mechanism for AUSSOM.
anchors.key: Welcoming adoption excludes opposition to that adoption. It does not settle whether France objected to any one funding mechanism.

anchors.card: Algeria did not participate in the vote on resolution 2797 (2025). It said the draft did not sufficiently reflect United Nations decolonization doctrine.
anchors.witness: Algeria did not participate in the vote on resolution 2797 (2025).
anchors.conflict: Algeria recorded an abstention on resolution 2797 (2025).
anchors.open: Algeria objected to the draft's treatment of decolonization.
anchors.key: Recorded abstention and nonparticipation in this roll call are distinct. A procedural choice can coexist with an objection to the text.

anchors.card: Pakistan sought a consensus-building approach during negotiations. Pakistan said the final text did not reflect that approach. Its recorded vote was an abstention.
anchors.witness: Pakistan said the final text did not reflect that approach.
anchors.conflict: Pakistan said the final text reflected the consensus-building approach it had advocated.
anchors.open: Pakistan said the negotiations made progress on some concerns.
anchors.key: The card resolves the pronoun to the same consensus-building approach. Failure to reflect that approach can coexist with progress on some concerns.

anchors.card: The United States urged talks using Morocco's autonomy proposal as the only basis for a just and lasting solution. It stated support for a mutually acceptable solution.
anchors.witness: The United States urged talks using Morocco's autonomy proposal as the only basis for a just and lasting solution.
anchors.conflict: The United States urged the parties to treat Morocco's autonomy proposal as one of several equally acceptable bases for talks.
anchors.open: The United States said it would reject an agreement that was not mutually acceptable.
anchors.key: An only basis excludes several equally acceptable bases. The choice of starting point leaves separate acceptance conditions open.
